frontmatter.goal: Develop an AI-powered journalism storage and accountability system

content.title: FTFM: AI-Powered Journalism Storage System
content.body:
## Project Overview
The FTFM project aims to create an AI-powered system that transforms journalism from its traditional report-based model into a structured, searchable database. The core functionalities include extracting and storing entities (people, places, events, policies), tracking public claims, and identifying contradictions in public statements.

### Key Features
- **Entity Extraction**: Automatically identify and categorize key entities from news sources.
- **Claim Tracking**: Monitor public statements over time.
- **Statement Half-Life**: Analyze how long statements remain unchallenged before being contradicted.
- **Narrative Collision Detection**: Detect conflicting narratives across different sources.
- **Credibility Scoring**: Assign scores to sources based on their history of accuracy.
- **AI & Graph Databases**: Use advanced AI models and databases for efficient information retrieval.

### Timeline & Priority
- **Priority**: High
- **Deadline**: January 1, 2025
- **Status**: Planning

### Next Steps
- Develop a proof-of-concept by extracting structured data from Glenn Greenwald’s podcasts.
- Expand the system to integrate additional sources and analytical tools.

### Related Notes
- [FTFM MVP Plan](MVP-Plan.md)
- [FTFM Technical Architecture](Technical-Architecture.md)

content.title: Extract Data from Glenn Greenwald's Podcasts
content.body:
## Research Request
This project aims to extract transcripts from Glenn Greenwald’s podcasts over the last six months and convert them into structured JSON data.

### Objectives
- **Transcribe Podcasts**: Generate accurate transcripts from audio sources.
- **Extract Named Entities**: Identify key people, organizations, and locations mentioned.
- **Identify Contradictions**: Cross-check statements with past claims.
- **Reference Evidence**: Link relevant sources.

### Timeline & Priority
- **Priority**: Medium
- **Due Date**: July 1, 2024
- **Status**: In Progress

frontmatter.goal: Develop a metric for tracking the longevity of public claims

content.title: Statement Half-Life Metric for Claim Validity
content.body:
## Concept Overview
To enhance accountability in public statements, the ‘Statement Half-Life’ metric tracks how long claims remain unchallenged before being revised or contradicted.

### Implementation
- **Data Collection**: Monitor statements over time.
- **Revision Tracking**: Identify when claims are modified or disproven.
- **Visualization**: Graph changes in claim validity.

### Potential Impact
- Enables tracking of evolving narratives in politics and journalism.
- Helps assess credibility and reliability of sources.

### Related Notes
- [FTFM Overview](../Projects/FTFM/Overview.md)

frontmatter.goal: Evaluate the feasibility of blockchain-inspired security models

content.title: Blockchain-Inspired Data Integrity for FTFM
content.body:
## Research Overview
This research evaluates the potential of using blockchain-inspired hashing mechanisms to ensure the immutability of high-value reports while maintaining storage efficiency.

### Proposed Approach
- **Hybrid System**: Use blockchain for critical reports while keeping general data in centralized storage.
- **Efficiency**: Balance security with database performance.
- **Verification Mechanisms**: Implement cryptographic proofs for data integrity.

### Related Notes
- [FTFM Overview](../Projects/FTFM/Overview.md)

content.title: FTFM Mobile Interface for Real-Time Citizen Journalism
content.body:
## Project Overview
This project aims to develop a mobile application that allows journalists and citizens to contribute real-time voice reports. These reports will be automatically transcribed and structured into the FTFM database.

### Key Features
- **Real-Time Transcription**: Convert voice reports into text.
- **Entity Extraction**: Identify key topics and events.
- **Instant Database Integration**: Store submissions in the FTFM platform.

### Project Timeline
- **Priority**: High
- **Deadline**: June 1, 2025
- **Status**: Planning

### Related Notes
- [FTFM Overview](Overview.md)
